Souers, Executive Secretary, National Security Council', alongside the Director of Central Intelligence. The Council's own first decisions route attendance and scheduling through the Executive Secretary, authorise him 'to control, supervise, and administer funds which have been or hereafter may be made available to the National Security Council, with full powers with respect thereto', and record that 'The affairs of the Council will be conducted with the utmost secrecy.'

label: Rear Adm. Sidney W. Souers
narrative: Souers held, in sequence, the two offices through which the postwar national security paper actually moved. He was the first Director of Central Intelligence, designated under the Presidential directive of 22 January 1946 that created the National Intelligence Authority and the Central Intelligence Group, and he served until 10 June 1946. From August 1947 he was the first Executive Secretary of the National Security Council, the civilian staff head the National Security Act of 1947 created by statute, and he held that post until January 1950. At the Council's first meeting on 26 September 1947 the Council routed attendance requests and meeting scheduling through him, gave him full powers over its funds, resolved that its affairs would be conducted with the utmost secrecy, and admitted the Director of Central Intelligence as an observer and adviser. The board argues at length about what the National Security Council was and was not shown and has no node for the man who built its secretariat. He is named in the MJ-12 Eisenhower Briefing Document, and that is not why he is here.

timeline.label: Truman creates the Central Intelligence Group and the post of Director of Central Intelligence
timeline.text: A Presidential directive on the coordination of foreign intelligence activities provides that personnel assigned from State, War and the Navy 'shall collectively form a Central Intelligence Group and shall, under the direction of a Director of Central Intelligence, assist the National Intelligence Authority', the Director to be designated by the President and to sit as a non-voting member of the Authority. Rear Adm. Sidney W. Souers is the first holder and signs as Director of Central Intelligence within two weeks.
